correctness.rationale: The projective boundary is smooth; a Laurent torus chart has equation \(1+s+s^m u^{-N}=0\). The valuation equality \(\gcd(m,N)=1\) proves integrality. Singular derivatives force \(p\mid N\) and exactly \(h\) distinct roots for \(N=p^a h\). The étale coordinate \(u^{-h}\) yields an exact \((2,p^a)\) cusp at every point. Its delta and Tjurina invariants and the arithmetic-genus correction prove the claimed formulas. The included checker was executed and returned VERIFY_OK for 73 finite prime-degree combinations; these computations are corroborative only.

value.rationale: An infinite classical plane-curve family exhibits wild cusp singularities precisely at primes dividing the symmetry integer. A uniform analytic local equation, total singular-scheme length, and exact normalization genus classify each bad fiber, including higher Frobenius powers; these invariants are needed to understand degeneration and cannot be read off solely from smoothness failure.
